findings.summary: CoreFoundation adds __CF_USER_TEXT_ENCODING to a process's environment. Observed: under an exact clean launch, the qualification interpreter (-I -S -B) sees six variables where a non-CoreFoundation tool sees five. M0 under E15, which requires os.environ == ENVIRONMENT, would refuse every time. The probe's exact process.env check would fail every start if the official node loads CoreFoundation; a different Node build on this host links it (not verified for the official one). The macOS environment predicate is never defined.

findings.summary: 'Binds the files the interpreter loads from outside the OS' is false as specified. Not bound: the Python.app executable that the launcher re-executes as the process image (strings), the pure-Python standard library and its bytecode, and pyvenv.cfg. LC_RPATH appears in the Python.app executable, the framework library and all 76 lib-dynload modules, yet section 7's rules cannot apply to these files and no Python-side rules exist. Run-time loads are not covered.

Main's driver has no readback selection, so 'Today, both drivers refuse' is false. The R04 consequence cites OK-ENG-009 section 4 (branches and leases) instead of section 3 items 2 and 4, calls a changed outcome 'unchanged', and pre-records R04's classification. It also misdescribes unittest: a failing setUpClass is one class error, with three methods not executed, not three method errors.
